h1: California Real Estate Exam Quiz & Practice Questions
subhead: Take a free practice quiz or point your phone at any California real estate exam question for an instant, explained answer — national principles and DRE-specific law, without the guesswork.
metaTitle: California Real Estate Exam Quiz & Practice Questions | Cambo
metaDescription: Free California Real Estate Salesperson Exam quiz and practice questions with instant, explained answers. National real estate principles plus California Real Estate Law, agency, and disclosure rules.
whyItWorks: California blends national real estate principles with a dense body of state-specific law — the Real Estate Law, agency disclosure duties, trust fund handling, and disclosure statutes like Transfer Disclosure Statements — and it's easy to answer a question correctly under a "general" rule while missing the California-specific twist the exam is actually testing. Cambo reads the exact scenario and explains which rule, national or California, the correct answer is built on.

sampleQuestions.q: Under California law, what document must most residential sellers provide to buyers disclosing known material facts about a property's condition?
sampleQuestions.a: The Transfer Disclosure Statement (TDS) — California Civil Code requires most residential sellers to disclose known material facts about the property's condition to prospective buyers, separate from other required disclosures like natural hazards.

sampleQuestions.q: A California real estate salesperson receives trust funds (like earnest money) on behalf of a buyer. What must the salesperson generally do with those funds?
options: Deposit them into their own personal checking account temporarily
Give them directly to the buyer's lender
Turn them over to their responsible broker or deposit into a trust account per DRE rules
Hold them in cash until closing
sampleQuestions.a: Turn the funds over to the responsible broker (or deposit into a neutral escrow/trust account) — California's Real Estate Law imposes strict trust fund handling rules, and a salesperson commingling trust funds with personal funds is a serious violation.

sampleQuestions.q: Which agency oversees real estate licensing and enforces the Real Estate Law in California?
options: California Bureau of Real Estate Appraisers
sampleQuestions.a: The California Department of Real Estate (DRE) — it licenses salespersons and brokers and enforces the Real Estate Law, distinct from CAR, which is a trade association, not a regulator.

sampleQuestions.q: On the national portion of the exam, which type of listing agreement gives one broker the exclusive right to a commission regardless of who finds the buyer?
sampleQuestions.a: An exclusive right-to-sell listing — the listing broker earns a commission no matter who ultimately produces the buyer, including the seller themselves, which distinguishes it from an exclusive agency listing.

sampleQuestions.q: A California seller's property is located in a designated high fire severity zone. What is the seller generally required to do?
options: Nothing — fire zone status is only relevant to insurance companies
Disclose this on the Natural Hazard Disclosure Statement
Personally pay for brush clearance before every showing
Obtain a fire marshal inspection before listing
sampleQuestions.a: Disclose it on the Natural Hazard Disclosure Statement — California law requires sellers to disclose whether a property lies within a state-mapped natural hazard zone, including high fire severity zones.

sampleQuestions.q: What is the maximum commission rate a California broker may legally charge on a residential sale?
options: There is no state-mandated maximum — commission rates are negotiable
sampleQuestions.a: There is no state-mandated maximum — commission rates in California (and nationally) are negotiable between the broker and client, and the exam tests this as a point antitrust law specifically protects.

faqs.q: How many questions are on the California real estate salesperson exam?
faqs.a: 150 multiple-choice questions, covering both national real estate principles and California-specific law, taken over a 3-hour testing window.

faqs.q: What score do I need to pass?
faqs.a: 70%, meaning at least 105 of the 150 questions answered correctly.

faqs.q: How many pre-licensing education hours does California require?
faqs.a: 135 hours across three DRE-approved courses: Real Estate Principles, Real Estate Practice, and one approved elective.

faqs.q: How many times can I retake the exam?
faqs.a: As many times as needed within your 2-year application window — California has no fixed retake limit — though you'll pay the exam fee again each attempt and must wait for your prior result before scheduling the next one.

faqs.q: Is Cambo affiliated with the DRE?
faqs.a: No. Cambo is an independent study tool, not produced or endorsed by the California Department of Real Estate.

faqs.q: Who administers the California real estate exam?
faqs.a: The exam is administered directly by the California Department of Real Estate at DRE testing locations, not by a third-party vendor like Pearson VUE.
